sections.label: Interests
sections.intro: What pulls you in? There are no wrong answers here.

sections.label: Skills
sections.intro: What you can do today. This is kept separate from what interests you.

sections.label: Work style
sections.intro: How you like to work and what matters to you.

questions.prompt: Which of these would you happily spend a free Saturday on?

options.label: Building a small app or website from scratch
options.nova: Building from scratch — noted. Making something that runs is a strong signal for the Build trail.

options.label: Digging through a dataset to see what it says
options.nova: Digging into a dataset: that points toward the Data trail. Curiosity about what numbers hide is the main ingredient.

options.label: Training a model or wiring up a chatbot
options.nova: Models and chatbots — the AI trail it is. I've also nudged Build and Data, since both help here.

options.label: Redesigning an app screen that annoys me
options.nova: Fixing a screen that annoys you is how a lot of designers start. Marking Design strongly.

options.label: Solving a capture-the-flag puzzle or breaking my own test system
options.nova: Breaking things on purpose, in a safe sandbox — that's the Security trail. I'm also giving Systems a small bump.

options.label: Setting up servers, a home lab or a network
options.nova: A home lab is a great Systems signal. People who like infrastructure often drift toward security too, so I noted a little of that.

options.label: Organising a team or event and making it run smoothly
options.nova: Making a group run smoothly is a real skill, and tech teams need it. That goes onto the People trail.

options.label: Making a game or a creative experiment
options.nova: A game or a creative experiment — Play trail. It usually pulls in Build and Design as well, so I added those.

questions.prompt: You get a month and freedom to pick one project. Which one do you start?

options.label: A budgeting app with charts and reminders
options.nova: A budgeting app mixes building with a bit of data and design. I noted all three.

options.label: A recommender that suggests films from what a user likes
options.nova: A recommender is close to what this very app does. AI and Data both get a boost.

options.label: A deliberately vulnerable web app, so I can learn to attack and fix it
options.nova: Building something to break it — smart way to learn. Security leads, with Build and Systems behind it.

options.label: A 2D platformer with my own levels
options.nova: A platformer needs code, art sense and game feel. Play is the main trail here.

options.label: A pipeline that collects public data daily and keeps it tidy
options.nova: Automating data collection is the quiet backbone of many data teams. Systems and Data both noted.

options.label: A redesign of a campus app, after interviewing students about it
options.nova: Interviewing real users first — that's what separates design from decoration. Design and People both go up.

questions.prompt: Which headlines would you actually click?

options.label: How attackers got into a company's network
options.nova: The how of a breach is the part defenders study. That adds to Security.

options.label: A new language model can do something unexpected
options.nova: New model capabilities catch your eye — AI trail. I also added a little Build, since someone has to turn them into apps.

options.label: Why a huge service went down for hours
options.nova: Outage post-mortems are Systems reading. Good sign if you enjoy working out why things fail.

options.label: A survey result that turns out to be misleading
options.nova: Spotting a misleading statistic is a Data instinct. Noted.

options.label: How a small team launched a product people love
options.nova: Product stories mix design, teamwork and building. I spread the credit across all three.

options.label: How an indie game was made by two people
options.nova: Indie game stories — Play trail, with a bit of Build.

questions.prompt: When you use an app, what do you notice first?

options.label: How it looks and how easy it is to use
options.nova: You notice look and ease first. That's a designer's eye, so Design goes up.

options.label: Whether it is fast and reliable
options.nova: Speed and reliability: Systems thinking. Noted.

options.label: What it knows about me and how it uses that
options.nova: Wondering what an app does with your data touches both Data and Security. I noted both.

options.label: Whether it could be hacked or misused
options.nova: Thinking about misuse before features — a very Security-minded habit.

options.label: Which parts feel smart or predictive
options.nova: Noticing the smart parts leans AI, and Data sits right behind it.

options.label: Whether it is fun to use
options.nova: Fun first. Play trail, with Design just behind.

questions.prompt: Something you built stops working. What do you do first?

options.label: Read the code and logs line by line
options.nova: Line-by-line debugging is the heart of Build. Good habit.

options.label: Check the numbers: when did it start, how often, who is affected
options.nova: Measuring before guessing is Data thinking, and it helps Systems work too.

options.label: Ask whether someone broke it on purpose
options.nova: Suspecting foul play first — a security mindset. Noted.

options.label: Look at the environment: servers, network, configuration
options.nova: Checking the environment before the code is classic Systems instinct.

options.label: Ask a teammate to pair up and talk it through
options.nova: Talking it through with someone is a real strength. People goes up.

options.label: Try different things quickly and see what happens
options.nova: Rapid experimenting is a Play-style approach. It works best if you also keep notes on what you tried.

questions.prompt: A college club needs a volunteer. You put your hand up for…

options.label: Building the club's website
options.nova: Building the site: Build, with a bit of Design.

options.label: Designing posters and the logo
options.nova: Posters and logos — Design trail, with a creative streak.

options.label: Analysing the sign-up and feedback data
options.nova: Analysing feedback is a Data task that also helps people. Both noted.

options.label: Running the team and talking to sponsors
options.nova: Leading and talking to sponsors: People trail, strongly.

options.label: Setting up the lab machines, Wi-Fi and accounts
options.nova: Keeping the lab running is Systems work, and it often teaches security basics too.

options.label: Organising the CTF or hackathon
options.nova: Organising a CTF or hackathon mixes Security, People and a bit of Play. All three noted.

questions.prompt: Which of these have you actually done, even at a beginner level?
questions.hint: Pick all that apply. 'None yet' is a fine answer.

options.label: Written a program or app beyond coursework
options.nova: Programs beyond coursework count a lot. Recorded as a Build skill.

options.label: Used SQL, a spreadsheet or pandas to analyse data
options.nova: Hands-on data work recorded as a Data skill.

options.label: Trained a model or called an AI/LLM API
options.nova: You've used AI tools directly. That goes in as an AI skill, plus a little Build.

options.label: Made mockups or prototypes (Figma or similar)
options.nova: Mockups count as real design practice. Recorded as a Design skill.

options.label: Tried CTFs, security labs or vulnerability write-ups
options.nova: Security lab time recorded as a Security skill.

options.label: Used Linux and the command line, Docker or deployed something
options.nova: Command-line and deployment experience: recorded as a Systems skill, plus a little Build.

options.label: Led a team, event or club activity
options.nova: Leading others recorded as a People skill.

options.label: Made a game, mod or creative coding piece
options.nova: Making a game or mod recorded as a Play skill, plus a little Build.

options.label: None of these yet
options.nova: That's a perfectly fine starting point. Your matches will lean on what interests you, and every career has a beginner path.

questions.prompt: How comfortable are you with programming today?

options.label: Just starting out
options.nova: Starting out is fine. I won't count it against any career; I only track what you've done.

options.label: I can solve small problems in one language
options.nova: Small problems in one language: a small Build point recorded.

options.label: I can build complete projects with several parts
options.nova: Complete multi-part projects: a solid Build skill, plus a little Systems.

options.label: I'm comfortable in more than one language and tools like Git
options.nova: Several languages and Git — strong Build skill recorded.

questions.prompt: How do you feel about maths and statistics?

options.label: I enjoy them and do well
options.nova: Comfort with maths helps in Data and AI work. Both recorded as skills.

options.label: Fine when I see a use for it
options.nova: Fine with a purpose behind it — a small Data and AI point recorded.

options.label: I would rather avoid heavy maths
options.nova: Plenty of strong careers lean less on maths. I've recorded a small point for Design and People instead, but this is not a verdict on what you can learn.

options.label: Long stretches of focused, heads-down building
options.nova: Long focused stretches suit building and infrastructure work.

options.label: Investigating a puzzle: logs, numbers, clues
options.nova: Investigating clues fits data and security work equally. Both noted.

options.label: Talking to users and teammates for much of the day
options.nova: Lots of conversation points to People-heavy roles, and Design too.

options.label: A mix: some building, some meetings, some thinking
options.nova: A mixed day keeps your options wide. Small points to Build, People and Data.

options.label: Sketching ideas and trying creative variations
options.nova: Sketching and variations: Design and Play, equally.

options.label: Analytical: I like logic, evidence and rigorous answers
options.nova: Analytical style recorded across Data, Security and Systems.

options.label: Creative: I like new ideas, looks and feel
options.nova: Creative style recorded across Design and Play.

options.label: Practical: I like making things that work
options.nova: Practical, make-it-work style: Build.

options.label: Social: I like helping groups get things done
options.nova: Social, group-focused style: People.

questions.prompt: How much of your work time would you like to spend with other people?

options.label: Mostly working on my own
options.nova: Mostly solo: I gave a small point to Build, Security and Data, which often allow long independent stretches. Every role still involves some teamwork.

options.label: A small team, with regular check-ins
options.nova: A small team with check-ins is how many product and engineering teams work. Small points to Build, Systems and Design.

options.label: Often, with lots of different people
options.nova: Working with many people often: People goes up, with Design behind.

questions.prompt: What matters most to you in a first role?

options.label: Learning technical depth quickly
options.nova: Wanting technical depth leans toward build-heavy, systems and AI roles.

options.label: Seeing real users use what I make
options.nova: Seeing users use your work points to product-facing roles.

options.label: Protecting people or keeping important systems safe
options.nova: Protecting people and systems: Security, with Systems behind it.

options.label: Finding insights that change decisions
options.nova: Insights that change decisions: Data, plus the People skill of getting heard.

options.label: Making something creative and expressive
options.nova: Creative expression: Play, with Design behind it.

options.label: Leading and shaping what a team builds
options.nova: Shaping what a team builds: a strong People signal.
